regime.label: Short-gamma drift narrows toward the 1100 flip inside a still-growing Protection build, 81 DTE
evidence: Cumulative net GEX turns positive only above the 1100 gamma flip; spot at 1055.1 sits 44.9 points below it, down from 60 points on 07-09, so dealers remain net short gamma even as the gap narrows.
Put OI at the far 910 strike jumped 937 contracts (+26%) to 4,536 in one session on 1,153 lots of volume - a live, Vol2Vol-confirmed protection build, not stale OI.
P/C OI ratio rose to a 6-day high of 1.32 (from 1.22) even as the future rallied 14.6 points, a classic protection-into-strength signature.
Call OI still exceeds put OI by 5,048 contracts in the immediate 1040-1110 band, a locally dampening influence even while the broader cumulative book stays net short gamma.

S50U26.today_summary: SET50 Sep futures (S50U26) closed at 1055.1, +14.6 points (+1.4%) on the day, still 44.9 points below the 1100 cumulative gamma flip even as that gap narrowed from 60 points on 07-09. Put OI at the far 910 strike jumped 937 contracts (+26%) to 4,536 on 1,153 lots of volume - the week's largest single-day protection build - pushing the P/C OI ratio to a 6-day high of 1.32. Dealers remain net short gamma on a cumulative basis, but call OI now exceeds put OI by 5,048 contracts in the immediate 1040-1110 band, a locally dampening influence keeping the tape between the 1050 near-put support and the 1080 call wall. ATM IV eased slightly to 14.9% (from 15.0%), still inside the week's 13.8-15.3% range.
what_changed: 910 put OI +937 contracts (+26%) to 4,536 on 1,153-lot volume, the week's largest single-day protection build.
P/C OI ratio +0.10 to 1.32 (6-day high); P/C volume ratio flipped from 0.88 to 1.18 as puts outtraded calls into the rally.
Futures +14.6 points (+1.4%) to 1055.1, narrowing the gap to the 1100 gamma flip to 44.9 points from 60 points the prior session.
Near-put support rolled up to 1050 from 1000 the prior session; the 1080 call wall held for a second day (1853 to 1844 OI).
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Max pain has held at 1040 for all 6 sessions since 06-27 despite futures swinging from 1049.6 (07-02) to 1065.5 (07-03) to 1040.4 (07-09) and back to 1055.1 today - a 25-point round trip with zero max-pain drift, confirming the anchor is structural rather than a live target at 81 DTE. The gamma flip has held near 1100 all week while spot has oscillated 45-70 points beneath it, keeping the book cumulatively short-gamma throughout, though today's rally closed that gap to its narrowest point of the window (44.9 points, versus 60 on 07-09). Total put OI is up 63% from 8,352 (07-02) to 13,633 today, with the 910 tail-put strike alone growing 107% (2,186 to 4,536) - a textbook Protection-zone signature of downside insurance layering in ahead of a longer-dated risk. ATM IV stayed range-bound (13.8-15.3%) all week with no directional trend, so the put build reads as steady hedging demand rather than a fear spike. The 25-delta skew widened from 1.4 (07-03) to 2.9 today, the week's high, consistent with accelerating put positioning even as price recovered.

strategies.name: Iron condor 970P/990P x 1090C/1110C
strategies.rationale: Price has held between the 1040 max-pain anchor and 1080 call wall all week, and the immediate 1040-1110 band is call-OI-heavy (+5,048 vs put OI there), a locally dampening influence even while the book stays cumulatively short-gamma below the 1100 flip; 14.9% ATM IV near the week's low and 81 DTE give ample theta runway to sell that established range at defined risk.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = wing width (20) - net credit, per side.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close beyond either short strike - below 990 or above 1090 - breaks the range thesis.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1010P/970P
strategies.rationale: The 910 put wall grew 937 contracts (+26%) in one session on 1,153 lots of volume - live, Vol2Vol-confirmed flow, not stale OI - and the P/C OI ratio hit a 6-day high of 1.32; a debit spread rides that same downside-hedge flow, which is also the flow consistent with the book's cumulative short-gamma reading, at a capped, defined cost instead of naked short-put risk.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid to enter the spread; no further margin exposure.
strategies.invalidation: A close back above the 1070-1080 near-call-wall zone removes the near-term case for continued downside-hedge flow.

S50U26.prediction: Bias is neutral with a mild bullish tilt while spot narrows the gap to the 1100 cumulative gamma flip (44.9 points, down from 60 on 07-09) and holds above the 1040 max-pain anchor; the locally call-heavy 1040-1110 band (+5,048 OI tilt) has kept the tape range-bound between the 1050 near-put support and 1080 call wall all week. A daily close above 1080 on rising call volume (already the chain's highest at 318 contracts) would test the 1100 flip / 1110 25-delta-call band and could shift the book to net long gamma; a reversal back below roughly 1030, where per-strike dealer gamma turns net negative again under the 910 put wall's weight, would risk faster downside acceleration. At 81 DTE, treat directional conviction as low.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and nothing here should be read as a signal to execute a position. SET50 index options are cash-settled on the index with no physical delivery, so any pull toward max pain (1040) or the gamma flip is a tendency, not a guarantee, and pinning mechanics here are structurally weaker than for physically-settled single stocks. This series is 81 days from expiry with OI still building, so directional conviction should stay low, and defined-risk structures still carry their full stated max loss.
